description: Executable current Kotlin/Swift parity truth for the correctness, persistence, recovery, shared-policy, and immediate example-app capabilities audited from the PR #3999 baseline.

capabilities.title: Platform-address balance callbacks preserve derivation identity

swift.reason: Swift persists platform-address balances, but the current ADDR-09 manual case covers watermark/double-credit behavior rather than derivation account/address identity across a conflict and restart. A targeted restart test is still required before this invariant is marked supported.

capabilities.title: Core input selection and reservation are atomic
Token amounts and costs preserve the full u64 domain

swift.reason: Swift preserves full-u64 balances without changing the installed SwiftData schema: the original Int64 balance column stores the UInt64 raw bits, while computed/API values, predicates, and in-memory ordering use unsigned semantics. Exact supply/balance formatting, token-metadata fallback, and per-token-decimal transition parsing are covered. It remains partial pending a durable device-store restart gate; there is intentionally no balanceHex column, backfill, or alternate iOS persistence path.

verification.command: cd packages/swift-sdk && xcodebuild test -scheme SwiftDashSDK -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -only-testing:SwiftDashSDKTests/TokenBalanceUInt64PersistenceTests
cd packages/swift-sdk && xcodebuild test -scheme SwiftDashSDK -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -only-testing:SwiftDashSDKTests/TokenBalanceUInt64PersistenceTests

verification.id: token schema preserves full u64 supplies as JSON numbers
cost may use the high half of u64

capabilities.title: Shielded wallets rebind after restart from persisted viewing keys

swift.reason: Swift wires FVK persist/load, but no named host process-death seedless-rebind gate exists in the current test plan.

kotlin.reason: Room v6 storage and fail-closed Kotlin callbacks are wired through the JNI persist/load/free vtable with fixed-size paired-allocation coverage, network scoping, purge, and migration tests. The remaining release gate is an instrumented seedless process restart that makes the mnemonic unavailable and proves native shielded rebind/sync from the stored FVK.

capabilities.title: Deferred contact-crypto queue survives restart

swift.reason: The in-memory drain works, but the FFI backend does not persist or cold-load the queue.

kotlin.reason: The in-memory drain works, but the JNI backend does not persist or cold-load the queue.

capabilities.title: Identity registration and top-up resume from tracked locks

swift.reason: Resume UI and filtering exist, but ID-16 remains a pending funded testnet gate.

kotlin.reason: Kotlin wrappers and screens now reach compiled JNI registration-resume, top-up-resume, and tracked-lock list/free bridges; JNI rejects generic invitation authority and frees list/managed handles on failure paths. Shared tests cover exact Built-transaction rebroadcast, typed consumed/untracked failures, top-up path rederivation after restart, and voucher rejection. Remaining release gates are Android external-function/device execution across process death plus resolver teardown and foreign-wallet error mapping.

verification.id: registration resume forwards same outpoint and false voucher flag then frees handle
registration rejects identity index that differs from tracked lock before JNI
bound topup for another identity is excluded while unbound topup remains eligible

capabilities.title: User-triggered compact-filter rescan

swift.reason: The wrapper and UI exist, but no dedicated named rescan test currently verifies the user-triggered height rewind.

kotlin.reason: The Kotlin wrapper and per-wallet Android UI reach the compiled JNI rescan bridge, and shared tests prove rewind-only behavior for known wallets with equal/forward no-ops and unknown-wallet rejection. A device smoke must still prove JNI typed-error mapping and running-next-tick/stopped-next-start consumption; process death before consumption intentionally loses the in-memory request and requires reissue.

verification.id: per wallet typed failures are collected without aborting other rewinds

capabilities.title: Complete contested-name discovery by identity

swift.reason: Swift consumes the cached array, but the baseline lacks a named completeness test for more than eight unknown names.

kotlin.reason: Kotlin now reaches compiled JNI sync and cached-array bridges; the cached array is copied under an RAII free guard, the UI preserves loading/error/unavailable state, and shared last-write-wins tests prove full replacement including resolved-to-empty snapshots. Android identity persistence still drops contested snapshots on restore, with no schema slot before reserved v8 invitations, and JNI allocation-failure/device plus process-restart gates remain.

verification.id: one shared sync returns complete cached snapshot beyond old eight label cap

capabilities.title: Canonical masternode endpoint discovery

swift.reason: Swift duplicates filtering/default-port/host parsing instead of consuming one shared typed result.

kotlin.reason: Kotlin duplicates filtering/default-port/host parsing instead of consuming one shared typed result. Its live network-aware path selects the port per network (443 for mainnet, 1443 otherwise); the hardcoded 443 for non-mainnet survives only in the legacy single-argument compatibility overload.

capabilities.title: Account-scoped Platform-address identity funding selection

swift.reason: The example app greedily packs address inputs instead of invoking a Rust account-scoped composite.

kotlin.reason: The shared addresses-with-balances query is fixed to the first Platform Payment account, while Android pre-enumerates those results and greedily packs inputs. There is no caller-selected account parameter or shared account-scoped composite.

swift.reason: The app-local quote now matches Drive for the u48 amount ceiling, single-price saturation, set-price checked overflow, zero prices, tier selection, and full-u64 costs. capabilities.title: Pending max-supply group proposals are discoverable

kotlin.reason: The Kotlin app discovers max-supply proposal positions, but GroupActionRuleEvaluator duplicates the host-side rule policy pending shared S3a authorization/proposal evaluation. The update transition itself is bridged; discovery is not yet a shared Rust decision.
